title: Reverse Bits
prompt:
Reverse the bits of a 32-bit integer.

**Example**: input `43261596` (`00000010100101000001111010011100`) → `964176192` (`00111001011110000010100101000000`).

*(Java `int` is signed, so results with bit 31 set appear negative. That is expected.)*

tests.note: bit 0 moves to bit 31 (the sign bit)

hints: Picture taking bits off one end of `n` and adding them to the other end of `result`. How many times do you repeat?
Then shift n right with the unsigned `>>>` so the sign bit doesn't spread into it.

solution.explanation: The result is built from the left while n is used up from the right. The first bit taken from n's bottom ends at the top of result after 31 more left shifts. Looping exactly 32 times (with `>>>`) handles negative inputs correctly. O(1) time (32 steps), O(1) space.
